title: Jesus' Instruction for ministry. Part 7
scripture_ref: 14 “If anyone will not welcome you or listen to your words, shake the dust off your feet when you leave that home or town.”
scripture_text: 15 “I tell you the truth, it will be more bearable for Sodom and Gomorrah on the Day of Judgment than for that town.”
devotional:
Matthew 10 5-15 gives us Jesus’ first instructions to the world’s first Christian missionaries. What Jesus says here is helpful for all missionaries, at all times and in all places.

They were under his instruction.

“These twelve Jesus sent out with the following Instructions” Matthew 10:5a

The Greek word for instructions is Parangello, which is a military term used to describe an order given by a commanding officer. It was an order that required unhesitating and unqualified obedience. It was a word used to describe an official court summons. It was used to describe a moral obligation. It was also used to describe a prescription from a doctor. So what Jesus saying here to these men is not merely some good ideas he has thought of, they are commands, they are things that he demands of us. They are instruction for Ministry.

These are instructions for a spiritual mission not for a ‘successful’ mission’

Often we are tempted into thinking that if we do everything Jesus commands us to do then our ministry is bound to be successful, but if you read this passage carefully they you will notice that Jesus spoke very little about success.

17 "Be on your guard against men; they will hand you over to the local councils and flog you in their Synagogues.”

18 “On my account you will be brought before Governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.”

19.”But when they arrest you do not worry about what to say or how say it.”

“Brother will betray brother to death, and a father his child; children will rebel against their parents and have them put to death.”

22 “All men will hate you because of me, but he who stands firm to the end will be saved.”

23 “When you are persecuted in one place, flee to another.

25 If the head of the house has been called Beelzebub, how much more the members of his household!”

26 "So do not be afraid of them.”

28 “Do not be afraid of those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul.”

34 "Do not suppose that I have come to bring peace to the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but a sword.

35 “For I have come to turn a man against his father, a daughter against her mother, a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law--”

36. “A man's enemies will be the members of his own household.'

In this chapter, Jesus give a realistic perception of ministry and the pressures of ministry. It is because of his realism that he gives these instructions. It is because of his love for his apostles that he gives these commandments. Knowing how to handle the stress and strain of ministry is more important than knowing how to be successful in ministry.
prayer: Father thank you that Jesus had more to say about how we cope with the stress of ministry than the success of ministry.
